newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end sharply down on cash weakness.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end sharply down on cash weakness.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed sharply lower to the three cent a lb limit down, weakened by reports that the cash market was turning lower.
USDA reported at midday that cash bellies were trading at $92 per cwt for 12-14 lb supplies, down $2 from Friday. The market had been on a strong uptrend, rising $10 last week.
"I'm hearing we will be down to $90 tomorrow (Tuesday)," one floor trader said.
The pool of unfilled sell-orders on the August contract, which finished the three cent limit down at 83.225 cents a lb, was estimated at 30 cars.
Other months ended 2.675 to 0.825 cent lower.
A slight pick-up in the pace of the hog slaughter appeared to have contributed to the turnaround in the cash market.
USDA reported a hog kill last week of 1.657 million head, up around two percent from the previous week.
Dealers noted there was little reaction to Friday's USDA cold storage report, which showed lower than expected frozen pork belly stocks, as of June 30.
The report put frozen belly stocks at 52.3 million lbs, below analysts' estimates which ranged from 53.5 million to 53.8 million lbs.

Hog futures closed mostly lower. The main exception was August, which was underpinned by strength in the cash market. USDA reported interior markets were $0.50 to $1.00 higher on Monday. Dealers said cash hogs would be steady-firm Tuesday.
Floor sources said Rosenthal Collins actively bought August/sold October. August closed 0.100 cent higher at 81.350 cents a lb. Other months were 0.900 cent lower to 0.050 cent higher.
